title: Optimal \(\ell_{1}\) distortion of binary edit distance
formal: For each integer \(n\ge2\), let \(X_n=\{0,1\}^{n}\) and define \[D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)=\inf\bigl\{D\in[1,\infty):\ \exists m\in\mathbb N_{\ge1},\ \exists f:X_n\to\mathbb R^m,\ \exists a>0,\ \forall x,y\in X_n,\ a\,\mathrm{ED}(x,y)\le\|f(x)-f(y)\|_1\le D a\,\mathrm{ED}(x,y)\bigr\}.\] Determine the asymptotic growth of \(D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)\) up to universal multiplicative constants as \(n\to\infty\).
definitions: The integer \(n\) is the length of each string; the metric space \(X_n\) contains \(2^n\) strings. The distance \(\mathrm{ED}(x,y)\) is the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions needed to transform \(x\) into \(y\), each at cost one. Inserted and substituted characters are binary, and intermediate strings may have any finite length. For \(v\in\mathbb R^m\), \(\|v\|_1=\sum_{i=1}^{m}|v_i|\). The dimension \(m\) is any finite positive integer, coordinates are arbitrary real numbers, and the map need not have an efficient or computable description. There is no bound on dimension or construction/evaluation time, and no requirement for a uniform algorithm across different \(n\). The same map \(f\) and positive scale \(a\) must satisfy both inequalities simultaneously for all pairs in \(X_n\); \(f,m,a\) may depend on \(n\). The infimum ranges over all such choices. Every finite metric space has a finite-distortion embedding into some finite-dimensional \(\ell_1\), so \(1\le D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)<\infty\).

context_blocks.text: The card retains the quantitative growth question adopted in its earlier review. This is an editorial broadening of asking only whether a polylogarithmic-distortion embedding exists: a matching asymptotic determination can settle either growth regime. It is not attributed to the source as an identically worded conjecture.

Ostrovsky and Rabani prove \(D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)\le 2^{O(\sqrt{(\log n)(\log\log n)})}\). This is a subpolynomial upper bound whose displayed growth exceeds every fixed power of \(\log n\). Their geometric theorem places no algorithmic constraint on the embedding. Here and in the asymptotic bounds, logarithms may be taken to base two and the displayed formulas concern sufficiently large \(n\).

Krauthgamer and Rabani prove \(D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)=\Omega(\log n)\). Together with the upper bound, this leaves a gap between logarithmic and subpolynomial distortion. Both of these papers explicitly include unit-cost substitutions, matching this card's distance.

The earlier Khot–Naor lower bound is \((\log n)^{1/2-o(1)}\), rather than logarithmic. That paper permits only insertions and deletions. If \(\mathrm{ED}_{\mathrm{indel}}\) denotes this convention, then \(\mathrm{ED}\le\mathrm{ED}_{\mathrm{indel}}\le2\mathrm{ED}\), so the two optimal distortion functions agree within a factor of two; they need not agree pointwise.

Near-linear-time constant-factor approximation of the distance between two supplied strings concerns a different mathematical guarantee. It does not give a single map of the entire binary-string metric into ordinary \(\ell_1\) with constant distortion.

The FOCS 2025 work develops average embeddings into similarity measures and obtains polylogarithmic approximation for edit-distance nearest-neighbor search. The primary abstract states this different target; it does not claim the all-pairs ordinary-l1 embedding required here.

why: Determining this distortion would explain how closely the geometry of binary sequence editing can be represented by sums of coordinate differences, closing a longstanding gap between metric embeddings and their obstructions.
answer_criterion: Specify a positive function \(h:\mathbb N_{\ge2}\to\mathbb R_{>0}\) describing the asymptotic growth, and give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean that there are absolute constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\) with \(c\,h(n)\le D_{\mathrm{ED}}(n)\le C\,h(n)\) for every integer \(n\ge2\). The proof must establish matching upper and lower bounds for the unrestricted embeddings and edit operations specified above. Merely repeating the defining infimum, computing a finite table, or giving unmatched upper and lower bounds does not determine the asymptotic order. A polylogarithmic upper bound alone need not meet this criterion. The required precision is multiplicative constant factors, as appropriate for the retained asymptotic-complexity question.

references.title: Low Distortion Embeddings for Edit Distance
references.locator: Author-hosted draft dated 19 August 2005. Section 2, PDF p. 4: insert/delete/substitute convention. Section 3, Theorem 7, PDF p. 7: unrestricted geometric embedding and distortion upper bound; Section 4, Theorem 10, PDF p. 13, separately treats efficient randomized evaluation. Preliminary STOC 2005 publication DOI 10.1145/1060590.1060623; later Journal of the ACM 54(5), article 23 (2007). The cited theorem numbers refer to this draft.

references.title: Improved lower bounds for embeddings into L1
references.locator: SODA 2006, pp. 1010–1017, author-hosted extended abstract. Section 1, PDF p. 1: edit distance includes substitutions. Theorem 1.2, PDF pp. 2–3: logarithmic distortion lower bound. Section 3, PDF pp. 6–7: proof and remaining gap. Later SIAM Journal on Computing 38(6), pp. 2487–2498 (2009), DOI 10.1137/060660126.

references.title: Nonembeddability theorems via Fourier analysis
references.locator: Author-hosted full manuscript for Mathematische Annalen 334(4), pp. 821–852 (2006). Section 1, PDF p. 3: insertion/deletion-only edit convention. Section 4, Theorem 4.1, PDF p. 12: the earlier (log n)^(1/2-o(1)) lower bound. Preliminary version appeared at FOCS 2005. This is not the source of the logarithmic lower bound.

references.title: Edit Distance in Near-Linear Time: it's a Constant Factor
references.locator: arXiv v2, revised 14 July 2022; original version 15 May 2020 and FOCS 2020 publication. Abstract and introduction, PDF pp. 1–3: a constant-factor approximation algorithm for a supplied pair of strings, using an input-dependent distance oracle. This is a different guarantee from an embedding of all binary strings into ordinary l1.

references.title: Embeddings into Similarity Measures for Nearest Neighbor Search
references.locator: FOCS 2025, pp. 864–893, conference 14–17 December 2025; added to IEEE Xplore 9 February 2026. Publisher abstract: average embeddings into similarity measures and polylogarithmic-approximation nearest-neighbor search for edit distance. Only the primary abstract and metadata were accessible in this review; no full-text theorem is attributed here.

progress.text: Ostrovsky and Rabani construct an embedding with distortion \(2^{O(\sqrt{(\log n)(\log\log n)})}\). The geometric existence theorem is separate from its efficient randomized implementation.
Khot and Naor publish the earlier \((\log n)^{1/2-o(1)}\) lower bound for insertion/deletion edit distance; the preliminary result appeared in 2005.
Krauthgamer and Rabani strengthen the lower bound to \(\Omega(\log n)\), including unit-cost substitutions. The journal version appeared in 2009.

The revised Andoni–Nosatzki preprint gives a near-linear-time constant-factor algorithm for a supplied pair of strings. This computational result does not determine unrestricted \(\ell_1\) distortion.

Andoni and Nosatzki obtain polylogarithmic-approximation nearest-neighbor search via average embeddings into similarity measures. The checked publisher abstract distinguishes these objects from bilipschitz embeddings into \(\ell_1\) or \(\ell_2\).

status_note: The primary embedding and nonembeddability papers leave a logarithmic-versus-subpolynomial gap. A bounded primary-source review through 16 September 2026 found no verified matching asymptotic determination for the stated binary, unit-substitution, unrestricted finite-dimensional l1 model. The checked 2022 approximation-algorithm paper and 2025 similarity-measure abstract concern different guarantees. The latter was available only as a primary abstract and metadata, not full text. This review is not an exhaustive certification of current openness. The retained constant-factor growth target is an acknowledged editorial broadening of the earlier polylogarithmic-existence question.

sentences: Binary edit distance counts unit-cost insertions, deletions and substitutions.
One map of all length-n strings into a finite-dimensional l1 space must preserve every distance within a common multiplicative distortion.
The dimension, real coordinates and computation needed to obtain the map are unrestricted.
Verified bounds range from logarithmic distortion to the Ostrovsky–Rabani subpolynomial upper bound.
The retained question asks for matching bounds within universal constant factors; recent distance algorithms and similarity-measure embeddings give different guarantees.

checked_sources: The sharp cited lower bound is due to Krauthgamer–Rabani, not Khot–Naor. Checked the former's actual SODA extended abstract, which includes insert/delete/substitute operations, and the latter's full manuscript, which permits only insertions/deletions. The factor-two equivalence preserves asymptotic order but not exact finite-n values.

Verified that both factors log n and log log n are inside the upper bound's square root. The upper draft's Section 3 explicitly separates geometric existence from computational efficiency; Theorem 10's pairwise probability is not silently substituted for the simultaneous all-pairs target of Theorem 7.

SODA 2010 Andoni–Jayram–Patrascu, Lower bounds for Edit Distance and Product Metrics via Poincare-Type Inequalities, introduction PDF p. 2, independently identifies the same l1 upper/lower bounds. Its new result is communication complexity, not an improved l1 distortion bound. Cached for the audit but omitted from the card's already sufficient reference list.

Read the 2022 arXiv v2 revision, not merely the 2020 date; its metric oracle depends on input substrings and is not a universal l1 embedding. Checked the 2025 FOCS paper's primary IEEE abstract and metadata: average similarity-measure embeddings and ANNS differ from ordinary l1 all-pairs distortion. Direct full-text retrieval was blocked; record that limitation rather than attributing an unseen theorem.

The FOCS 2025 publication was added to IEEE Xplore in February 2026, which does not make it a new 2026 theorem. Bounded 2025/2026 searches found no primary result establishing the requested matching asymptotic growth. Unverified secondary summaries were not used as mathematical evidence.
